summary: An indologist and religious studies scholar, John Woodroffe studied at University College, Oxford. He served as a Judge at the Calcutta High Court, Fellow and Tagore Law Professor at the University of Calcutta, and Reader in Indian Law at Oxford.

Join Saeki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Sennyu-ji and under Jocho Chihaya. He held posts at Kangakuin, the University of Tokyo, the Japan Academy, and served as chief abbot (管主) of Horyu-ji from 1903 to 1950.

Jokai Hiraoka, a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology, studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo (~1947–1953). He held academic posts at Shuchiin University and served as professor at Otemae University (~1966–1988).

Jon Kabat-Zinn studied at Haverford College and MIT (Ph.D. ~1965–1971), learning under Philip Kapleau, Thích Nhất Hạnh, Seungsahn Haengwon, Jack Kornfield, and Joseph Goldstein. He held posts at the Insight Meditation Society and the University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School.

Jonardon Ganeri studied at Cambridge, King's College London, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. Specializing in philosophy and indology, he held appointments at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash, NYU, and became Bimal K. Matilal Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at Toronto.

Jonathan A. Silk studied at Oberlin, Kyoto, Ryukoku, and Michigan (Ph.D. under Luis O. Gómez). A scholar of Buddhist studies, indology, and tibetology, he held posts at Western Michigan, Yale, UCLA, Leiden, Göttingen Academy of Sciences, and Minobusan University.

Jonathan C. Gold is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and tibetology. He has held teaching posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies in East Asian Languages and Civilizations at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and served as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

Jonathan Geen, a scholar of indology and religious studies, completed his doctorate at McMaster University in 2001 under Phyllis Granoff. He has held teaching positions at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover studied at Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford. A philosopher, he served as a fellow and tutor at New College, Oxford (~1965–1996), and held posts at King's College London (~1996–2013), Hastings Center, and Oxford.

Jonathan Karam Skaff studied at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and Xiaofu Wang, and earned a PhD at Michigan. A scholar of sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history, he joined Shippensburg University and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Philosopher Jonathan Lear studied at Yale, Cambridge, Rockefeller University (Ph.D.), and Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis. He held academic posts at Yale, Cambridge, Clare College, and the University of Chicago (2014–2022).

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is a scholar of history, archaeology, and indology. Educated at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley, he became the George F. Dales Jr. & Barbara A. Dales Professor of Anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Jonathan Z. Smith studied at Haverford, Yale, and Yale Divinity School. A religious studies scholar, he held posts at Dartmouth, UC Santa Barbara, served as president of the Society of Biblical Literature, and was Dean of the College at Chicago.

Jong Cheol Lee studied at Seoul National University and earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima. Active in Buddhist studies and indology, he held posts at the University of Mysore and the Academy of Korean Studies.

Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and indology. He studied at Shitennoji University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg in 1998 under the supervision of Lambert Schmithausen.

Jongmyung Kim studied at Yonsei, Seoul National University, and UCLA (under Robert E. Buswell Jr.). Focusing on Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and religious studies, he served as Associate Professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

Joryu Chiba studied national history at Ryukoku University, later serving there as assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor emeritus. He also held posts at Kyoto Women's University, Ryukoku Daigaku Shigakkai, Honganji Historical Materials Research Institute, and Soai Gakuen.

Jos Gommans studied at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink. A historian and indologist, he held posts at the Dutch Research Council, the Kern Institute, and Leiden University.

Josef Horovitz, a scholar of religious studies, linguistics, and history, completed his doctoral studies under Eduard Sachau (~1895–1898). He subsequently held a post at Goethe University Frankfurt from ~1914 to 1931.
